xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.title: Homes Taken for Xi'an Ring Roads and the Weiyang Palace Road, With Payments Left Late
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.place: Weiyang Palace site in the Han Chang'an City area and the Second Ring Road interchange at Xinjiamiao, Weiyang District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, with further works in Huxian (Huyi) District, China
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.point: The Han Chang'an City Weiyang Palace national archaeological site park, Weiyang District, Xi'an, where the project rebuilt a Han Dynasty road network and where 37 households were still waiting for replacement housing when the loan closed (OpenStreetMap point for the Weiyang Palace archaeological park)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-75580 for the Xi'an Sustainable Urban Transport Project (P092631). US$150 million, approved 24 June 2008, effective 24 December 2008, fully disbursed. Environmental category A. Original closing 30 June 2015; actual closing 31 March 2017 after two restructurings, on 22 December 2014 and 30 June 2016. The completion report's restructuring table gives the reason for the second restructuring as 'Delayed resettlement of 76 households' and records that the closing date was extended by nine months 'to allow completion of the resettlement'. The loan financed improvements to Xi'an's First and Second Ring Roads and Taibai Nan Road, the upgrading of four roads in Huxian, two passenger transport terminals and a bus depot, an area traffic control system, an air quality monitoring centre and laboratory, the re-creation of a Han Dynasty road network in the Weiyang Palace area and bicycle routes linking tourist sites. The project ran to 47 sub-components and 114 contracts at appraisal, 87 in the end. The completion report of 20 September 2017 rated outcome Moderately Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Moderate, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory, with quality at entry Moderately Unsatisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, dated 5 March 2018 in the Bank's archive record, also reached Moderately Satisfactory on outcome, on a split rating of moderately unsatisfactory before the 2015 restructuring and moderately satisfactory after, weighted 40/60 by disbursement to 3.6; it rated risk to development outcome Modest and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004130, 20 September 2017; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, CN-Xi'an Sustainable Urban Transport).

companies.name: Xi'an Project Management Office
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet. It coordinated eleven Xi'an municipal bodies listed in the completion report: the Development and Reform Commission, Finance Bureau, Planning Bureau, Construction Bureau, Environmental Protection Bureau, Communication Bureau, Civil Administration Bureau, National Land and Resources Bureau, Cultural Heritage Bureau and Public Security Bureau, together with the Xi'an Infrastructure Implementation Corporation. A separate project management office in Huxian handled the four county road sub-components; the completion report records weaknesses in its financial management system (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 20 September 2017).

xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.community: The project widened and rebuilt ring roads and interchanges across Xi'an and built a Han Dynasty road network inside the Weiyang Palace archaeological area. The completion report gives the outcome of the land take: 918,700 square metres of land, or 1,378 mu, was acquired, 152,000 square metres (228 mu) less than originally planned, and 99,945 square metres of houses and buildings were demolished. A total of 2,371 households, 11,433 people, were resettled under the project. The report states this is significantly more than the 527 households and 4,770 people estimated at appraisal, and attributes the difference to changes in the project design. Payments to 39 households in Xinjiamiao village and to 37 households at the Weiyang Palace construction site were delayed, and the completion report says those delays caused the second extension of the loan closing date. The 39 households at Xinjiamiao took monetary compensation and were paid in full by 31 December 2016. The 37 households at the Weiyang Palace site chose new housing rather than cash and were left waiting for the resettlement site to be built; the completion report, written in September 2017, says they would continue to receive transition subsidies until they moved to their permanent houses and that they would move no later than March 2018. That is more than nine months after the loan closed on 31 March 2017. The report rates social safeguards implementation Moderately Satisfactory and says the resettlement plan and policy framework were complied with. It also records that the project's one-year and nine-month closing extensions were needed to finish the resettlement, and that the project's appraisal underestimated the scale of resettlement required. The Evaluation Group's review repeats the same figures and adds that the Bank team may have underestimated the risk that resettlement posed to timely implementation.
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.displaced_label: people resettled under the project, 2,371 households in all (World Bank completion report, 20 September 2017)
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,100 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved; no figure of 2,100 was found in any Bank document opened. The Bank's completion report gives an outcome of 2,371 households, 11,433 people, resettled, against an appraisal estimate of 527 households and 4,770 people. The 11,433 is an outcome figure in the completion report, not a reprint of the appraisal plan, and the report itself sets the two side by side.
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 March 2017 with 37 households at the Weiyang Palace site still in transitional housing, due to move by March 2018. The completion report says monitoring and reporting were continuing to ensure that all households were resettled according to the resettlement action plan. No document found records whether the 37 households moved on that date. A follow-up Bank operation, the Shaanxi Xi'an Intelligent Public Transport Project (P157787), was under preparation when the completion report was written.

xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.confidence_note: Every figure here comes from the Bank's own completion report, the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report, the appraisal document and the project agreement. The lender is reporting on its own project. No independent press account, court record, audit or field study of this resettlement was found; two searches, one of them in Chinese for the named village, returned nothing on these works. The completion report names no affected person, gives no compensation rate, does not say how long the payments to the 39 and the 37 households were late, and does not break the 11,433 people down by site. It states that the resettlement plan and policy framework were complied with and rates social safeguards implementation Moderately Satisfactory. The two Bank documents also differ on one rating: the completion report gives risk to development outcome as Moderate and the Evaluation Group's review gives it as Modest. The Evaluation Group's review prints no date anywhere on the page; the date given for it is the Bank archive's own record field, which is not verified on the document itself.
xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.conditions: The project was environmental category A and triggered the policies on environmental assessment, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement. The Project Agreement for Loan 7558-CN, dated 29 September 2008, required the implementing entity, where acquisition of land or assets or displacement of people was unavoidable, to make compensation available in accordance with the resettlement action plans and the resettlement policy framework 'before the carrying out of the works which would result in such acquisition or displacement', in a manner satisfactory to the Bank. It also barred amendment, suspension or waiver of the plans without the Bank's prior concurrence, and made activities under three parts of the project ineligible for financing unless a resettlement action plan for them had been prepared under the policy framework and approved by the Bank. The completion report records that payments to 39 households at Xinjiamiao and 37 at the Weiyang Palace site were delayed, and that the delay forced the nine-month extension of the closing date (Project Agreement, 29 September 2008; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 20 September 2017).

wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.title: Years in Transitional Housing for Families Moved Off the Jiefang Avenue Extension
wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.place: Nanhu Village resettlement site, Huangpi District, Wuhan, Hubei, with works also on the Jiefang Avenue Extension and the Shuidong section of the Second Ring Road, China
wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.point: Huangpi District, Wuhan, the district that built and was responsible for the Nanhu Village resettlement site and whose approval delays left families in transitional housing (OpenStreetMap administrative point for Huangpi District; the village itself is not mapped at a point that could be confirmed)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-78640 for the Wuhan Second Urban Transport Project (P112838). US$100 million, approved 30 March 2010, effective 7 September 2010, fully disbursed. Environmental category B. Original closing 31 December 2015; actual closing 31 August 2018 after restructurings on 26 June 2015 and 30 August 2017. Total project cost rose from US$610.71 million at appraisal to US$926.82 million, the borrower's own contribution rising from US$510.71 million to US$826.82 million. The loan financed the Jiefang Avenue Extension, the elevated and ground sections of the Shuidong stretch of the Second Ring Road, the Tianshunyuan and Sanjintan public transport terminals and bus corridor works. The completion report of 28 June 2019 rated outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and quality of monitoring and evaluation Modest. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, dated 18 November 2019 in the Bank's archive record, recommended the project for a field-based assessment alongside two other Chinese urban transport projects (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 28 June 2019; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, CN-Wuhan Second Urban Transport).

companies.name: Wuhan Urban Construction Utilization of Foreign Investment Project Management Office
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet, the unit of the Wuhan municipal construction administration that handles foreign-financed urban works. Land acquisition and resettlement were not run from it: the completion report states the resettlement work was subproject and district based and was carried out by the acquisition and compensation departments of the district in which each subproject sat, with Huangpi District in charge of building the Nanhu Village resettlement site (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 28 June 2019).

companies.name: Center for Involuntary Resettlement Research, Wuhan University
companies.role: The independent monitor required by the resettlement action plan. It monitored the project's resettlement work and submitted 16 external monitoring reports to the Bank between January 2011 and July 2018 (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 28 June 2019). None of those 16 reports was found in the Bank's document archive.

wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.community: The project built the Jiefang Avenue Extension and the Shuidong section of Wuhan's Second Ring Road, with works scattered across the city. The completion report records that 7 urban residential communities and 21 suburban villages were affected in various degrees by land acquisition and house demolition, that the project affected 1,055 families with 3,265 people and 40 enterprises, and that it required 31 hectares of land and nearly 300,000 square metres of structures. The resettlement plan was updated for the Nanhu Village Interchange sub-project of the Jiefang Avenue Extension, with a demolition area of 116,700 square metres, which the report says made this the largest-scale resettlement among the Bank's transport projects in China at the time. Three resettlement sites were used, and the report's account of them differs sharply by site. At the Shuidong section, all displaced families received full compensation, annual village royalty payments from village business profits, several apartments each on average, and social security and medical insurance as they became urban residents. On the Jiefang Avenue section, where some displaced families included laid-off workers and some were below the urban poverty line, the resettlement works took over six years until every displaced family was relocated to their new apartments. At the Jiefang Avenue Extension section, Huangpi District was in charge of the Nanhu Village resettlement site, 1,500 apartments serving this project and three municipally funded projects. The land approval, design and urban planning of that site were delayed for over three years because the area had been taken into a new city, the Yangtze River Eco-city, approved by the State Council in 2016, which voided the earlier land-use planning. Without fresh land-use approval, the site's electricity, drinking water and gas could not be connected to the mains, and a plant to treat the new city's wastewater was still outstanding when the report was written. Resettlement at Nanhu Village was still unfinished when the loan closed on 31 August 2018 and when the completion report was written in June 2019; Huangpi District was paying the residents the stipulated transition fee. The report says the residents were aware of the delay and their entitlements and had expressed their understanding of the situation. Escalating land acquisition and resettlement costs ran through the project: the cost rose from US$192 million estimated at appraisal to US$520 million, an increase the completion report puts at 183.6 per cent and attributes mostly to rising real estate prices in Wuhan and in China generally. The Evaluation Group's review records that the shortage of counterpart funds to pay those costs delayed the Jiefang Avenue Extension and that the second extension of the closing date was due to slow resettlement in Huangpi District and delayed land acquisition for the two public transport terminals. The Bank's own grievance redress service received no complaints from citizens, and the final Bank supervision mission in March 2019 concluded that social safeguards were Satisfactory.
wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,486 for this project. That is to the person the appraisal plan figure: the Project Appraisal Document of 2 March 2010 states that 'Housing demolition will entail the relocation of 391 households with 1,486 people, 218 shops (with 556 employees), and 21 enterprises'. It is not a count of people moved. The completion report's outcome figures are larger in households and structures and smaller in land: 1,055 families with 3,265 people and 40 enterprises affected, 31 hectares of land against 48.2 hectares planned, and nearly 300,000 square metres of structures. The completion report's verb for the 1,055 families is 'affected', not relocated, and no Bank document found gives a count of people actually relocated, either in total or at any one of the three resettlement sites.
wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.outcome: The loan closed on 31 August 2018 with the Nanhu Village resettlement unfinished. The project management office and the Bank agreed that resettlement would be monitored every three months and that all families would be relocated to their new housing by June 2020, with the Bank monitoring that under a later operation, the Wuhan Integrated Transport Development Project. No document found records whether the families moved by that date. The Evaluation Group recommended the project for a field-based assessment; no Project Performance Assessment Report for it was found in the Bank's archive.

wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.confidence_note: The demolition areas, the three-year and six-year delays, the missing electricity, water and gas at the Nanhu Village site and the cost increases all come from the Bank's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it. The lender is reporting on its own project. No independent account of the Nanhu Village resettlement was found; two searches, one of them in Chinese for the village and the road, returned nothing on these works. The 16 external monitoring reports the completion report relies on are not in the Bank's public archive, so the figures cannot be checked against them. The report does not say how many families were at the Nanhu Village site, how many were still in transitional housing when the loan closed, how long any one family waited, or what the transition fee was. It states that the residents had expressed their understanding of the delay, that the Bank's grievance service received no complaints, and that the final supervision mission rated social safeguards Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's review prints no date anywhere on the page; the date given for it is the Bank archive's own record field, which is not verified on the document itself.
wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.conditions: The project was environmental category B and triggered the policies on environmental assessment and involuntary resettlement. The Project Agreement for Loan 7864-CN, dated 11 June 2010, required Wuhan, where acquisition of land or assets or displacement of people was unavoidable, to do two things 'before initiating the implementation of any works which would result in such acquisition or displacement': make compensation available and, as applicable, 'relocate and rehabilitate the displaced people in permanent sites with adequate facilities, including providing all related assistance required in respect thereof', in accordance with the resettlement action plan; and, where the relocation and rehabilitation assistance provided was of a transitory nature, 'make arrangements prior to implementing any such works for the permanent and adequate relocation and rehabilitation of such people in accordance with the RAP', on a time schedule satisfactory to the Bank. A further clause required Wuhan to carry out measures satisfactory to the Bank for improving the living standard of displaced persons. The completion report records that at the Nanhu Village site the electricity, drinking water and gas could not be connected, that the site's approvals were delayed for over three years, and that resettlement there was still outstanding when the loan closed and when the report was written ten months later (Project Agreement, 11 June 2010; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 28 June 2019).

qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.title: Households Relocated for the Qingyang Ring Roads as Resettlement Costs Tripled
qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.point: Xifeng District, the Qingyang city district holding all six sub-projects in the completion report's land acquisition table (OpenStreetMap place point for Xifeng District, Qingyang)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-81700 for the Gansu Qingyang Urban Infrastructure Improvement Project (P123133). US$100 million, approved 31 May 2012, effective 24 September 2012, fully disbursed. Environmental category B. Original closing 31 December 2017; actual closing 30 November 2019 after restructurings on 23 August 2016 and 10 October 2018. The loan financed urban roads in Xifeng District - the west section of Anding Road, the middle and south sections of Qinghua Road forming the west ring road, the north section of Beijing Road forming the east ring road and the east section of Guxiang Lu - together with the Dongqu wastewater treatment plant, drainage and wastewater management and transport action plans. The completion report of 21 May 2020 rated outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and quality of monitoring and evaluation Modest; the Independent Evaluation Group's review, dated 10 November 2020 in the Bank's archive record, reached the same three ratings (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 May 2020; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, CN-Gansu Qingyang Urban Infrastructure).

companies.name: Qingyang Project Management Office
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet. Under the project agreement the loan was made available through Gansu province to Qingyang Municipality and Xifeng District, with a project implementation unit in the Xifeng Housing bureau and another in the municipal water company. The municipal resettlement office supervised land acquisition and resettlement (Project Appraisal Document, 30 April 2012; Project Agreement for Loan 8170-CN, 12 July 2012; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 May 2020).

companies.name: Qingyang Municipal Water Supply and Sewage Company
companies.role: The municipal utility responsible for the wastewater component, one of the six sub-projects in the land acquisition table. The project included a covenant requiring it to furnish a financial performance improvement plan and to break even; the completion report records late delivery of that plan and an operating ratio of less than one (Project Appraisal Document, 30 April 2012; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 May 2020).

qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.community: The project built ring roads and a wastewater treatment plant on the edge of Xifeng District, the city district of Qingyang. The completion report sets out the outcome in a table of land acquisition and resettlement by sub-project: 800.66 mu of land acquired permanently, 324.1 mu occupied temporarily, 2,149 households affected and 226 households relocated. The relocations fell on three of the six sub-projects: 14 households on the west section of Anding Road, 114 on the north section of Beijing Road, 90 on the south section of Qinghua Road and 8 at the Dongqu wastewater works. The report also records that 640 households affected by house demolition and the removal of attachments were paid RMB466.3 million, that RMB53.27 million was paid to affected villages and individuals for permanent acquisition and temporary occupation together, and that the total cost of land acquisition and resettlement came to RMB520 million, 229 per cent more than the estimate in the resettlement action plan. A church and 35 household graves were relocated during road construction. The design of the street on West Anding Road was changed to avoid resettling an elderly landlord who refused to move and who, a photograph caption in the report says, refused any compensation plan. The resettlement ran years behind: by March 2015 only one of the project's 10 civil works contracts had completed land acquisition and resettlement, because land approvals given by Qingyang Municipality were not valid under a new land policy and had to be escalated to provincial level, and an audit of the municipal land bureau suspended the issue of land preview notes. Once the approvals came, the availability of local funds to pay for the resettlement became an issue alongside the growing cost. The 2016 restructuring cancelled two sub-projects - the final kilometre of the Western Ring Road and the purchase of vehicle equipment - to relieve the pressure on counterpart financing created by the rise in resettlement costs. The completion report also states that all affected households of the six sub-projects signed compensation agreements, received compensation and have been rehabilitated, that all temporarily occupied land was restored and returned, that ten monitoring reports concluded the resettlement plan was implemented satisfactorily and all affected people received the compensation due to them, and that a sample survey by the external monitoring team found the income and living conditions of affected people improved significantly after resettlement. The Evaluation Group's review puts it as 'the project affected 2,149 households, and 226 households were satisfactorily relocated'.
qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.displaced_label: households relocated, from the "Number of Relocated households" column of Table 4 (World Bank completion report, 21 May 2020)
qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,800 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved; no figure of 1,800 was found in any Bank document opened. The appraisal document estimated 740 mu of permanent land acquisition in eight villages in five townships, affecting 201 families or 862 people by land acquisition and 143 families by structure demolition; the appraisal gives the people in those 143 families as 528 in one passage and 529 in another. The completion report's outcome figures are larger throughout: 800.66 mu acquired, 2,149 households affected, 640 households affected by house demolition and attachment removal, and 226 households relocated. No Bank document found converts the 226 relocated households into a number of people.
qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.outcome: The loan closed on 30 November 2019 with the roads and the wastewater plant built and the resettlement complete. The completion report records that the plant's capacity had been miscalculated and that an emergency 10,000 cubic metre pool was to be built south of it before the 2020 rainy season to handle emergencies. The two cancelled sub-projects were not built with Bank money.

qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.confidence_note: The 226 relocated households, the 2,149 affected households, the land areas, the compensation sums and the 229 per cent cost increase all come from the Bank's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it. The lender is reporting on its own project. No independent account of this resettlement was found; two searches, one of them in Chinese, returned nothing on these works. The ten monitoring reports the completion report relies on are not in the Bank's public archive. The completion report names no affected person, gives no compensation rate per household, does not say how long any household waited, and does not convert the 226 relocated households into people. Both Bank documents state that all affected households received their compensation and that incomes and living conditions improved after resettlement, and the Evaluation Group's review calls the 226 relocations satisfactory. The elderly landlord who refused to move is described only in a photograph caption and a single sentence, with no name and no date. The Evaluation Group's review prints no date anywhere on the page; the date given for it is the Bank archive's own record field, which is not verified on the document itself.
qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.conditions: The project was environmental category B and triggered the policy on involuntary resettlement; the policy on indigenous peoples was not triggered, because a socio-economic survey found no indigenous community in the project area. A resettlement action plan was prepared, reviewed and disclosed before appraisal, advertised in local newspapers, posted on the Qingyang government website and held at the Qingyang Municipal Library free of charge. The Project Agreement for Loan 8170-CN, dated 12 July 2012, required Gansu, through Qingyang Municipality and Xifeng District, to implement the resettlement action plan and the environmental management plan according to their terms, and to 'ensure that all land acquisition under the RAP required for the purposes of carrying out works under the Project are financed exclusively out of Qingyang Municipality's and Xifeng District's resources' and to 'provide, promptly as needed, the resources needed for this purpose'. It also required semi-annual monitoring reports to the Bank from 15 March 2013, each detailing any conditions interfering with implementation and the remedial measures taken, and barred amendment or waiver of either plan without the Bank's prior written agreement. Each civil works contract had to oblige the contractor to implement the environmental management plan. The completion report records that the availability of local funds to finance the resettlement became an issue as its cost grew, and that two sub-projects were cancelled in 2016 to relieve the pressure on counterpart financing (Project Agreement, 12 July 2012; Project Appraisal Document, 30 April 2012; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 May 2020).

xining-wusixi-road-demolition.title: Houses Pulled Down Three Years Before the Replacement Flats Were Built in Xining
xining-wusixi-road-demolition.place: Taobei, Wangjiazhai and Wuzhong villages and the Wusixi Road and Xicheng Avenue corridor, Chengbei District, Xining, with works also in Huangzhong County, Qinghai, China
xining-wusixi-road-demolition.point: Chengbei District, Xining, the district in which the completion report says the entire project was located and in which the Taobei and Wangjiazhai resettlement complexes were built (OpenStreetMap administrative point for Chengbei District)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-83190 for the Qinghai Xining Urban Transport Project (P127867). US$120 million, approved 27 December 2013, effective 21 May 2014, revised to US$115,551,102 and that amount disbursed. Environmental category B. Original closing 30 September 2019; actual closing 30 August 2021 after restructurings on 26 September 2019 and 27 May 2021. Total project cost US$228,381,102, of which the borrower provided US$112,830,000. The loan financed new urban roads on the Wusixi Road corridor - Xicheng Avenue, 3.64 km with three bridges and an underpass; Wusixi Road, 3.43 km; and No. 5 Road, 1.02 km - dedicated bus lanes, stops and a public transport interchange, buses, an area traffic control system and studies and training. The 2019 restructuring added upgrades to Qiyi, Delingha, Bayi and Wuyi roads, 73 electric bus charging points and a relocated passenger station, and moved the public transport interchange from Yanxiaocun to Wangjiazhai. The completion report states flatly that 'The project did not finance land acquisision'; the city put US$83.7 million of its own counterpart funding into resettlement-related activities. The completion report of 22 February 2022 rated outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and quality of monitoring and evaluation Substantial; the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 29 June 2022 reached the same three ratings (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005538, 22 February 2022; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, China - Qinghai Xining Urban Transport Project).

companies.name: Xining Municipal Government
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet, working through a project management office. The completion report records that the Chengbei district government provided guidance and support in obtaining upper-level approvals for urban planning and urban land use and monitored the quality of the resettlement apartment construction, and that village committees ran much of the resettlement work - the impact survey, the collection of farmers' concerns, choosing the designer of the resettlement sites, organising their construction, and distributing apartments to affected families (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 22 February 2022).

companies.name: Xining Chengtong Transportation Construction & Investment Co., Ltd.
companies.role: The project implementing unit, the Xining municipal investment company that coordinated the January 2018 field survey and public consultation for the updated resettlement action plan (Resettlement Action Plan, January 2018).

companies.name: Involuntary Resettlement Research Center, China Three Gorges University
companies.role: The resettlement consulting agency that carried out the field survey and public consultation for the updated resettlement action plan between 7 and 20 January 2018 (Resettlement Action Plan, January 2018).

xining-wusixi-road-demolition.community: The project built new roads and a bus corridor across the northern edge of Xining. The appraisal document described two kinds of land take. The first was work treated as relevant to the project but carried out before the project was identified: a due diligence review covered the demolition of 520,487 square metres of houses, the acquisition of 368 hectares of land and the resettlement of 760 households during 2010 to 2012, and concluded those activities followed Chinese land law and Qinghai provincial and local regulation, with living conditions restored. The second was the land take for the project itself. The appraisal estimated 52.8 hectares of land across six villages in Chengbei District and Huangzhong County, 481 households and 1,921 people affected by land acquisition, the demolition of 150,661 square metres of structures displacing 121 households and 527 people, and the demolition of a further 5,792 square metres in seven enterprises. The updated resettlement action plan of January 2018 gives the outcome, citing the external monitoring agency's report: the land acquisition and structure demolition of the project had all been completed by 31 December 2016, with 233,600 square metres of structures demolished and 724.88 mu of land acquired, excluding the passenger station. The same document then records that the construction of the resettlement complexes was about three years later than the original plan. Construction of the Taobei Village resettlement complex was only started in October 2017, that of the Wangjiazhai Village complex in November 2017, and that of the Huangzhong County complex had not yet been started at all when the plan was written in January 2018 - more than a year after the houses came down. The completion report, written four years later, states that all resettlement sites were completed before the loan closed, that each family received at least two apartments, that villagers live in the same community without disruption to their original neighbourhoods, and that savings from building the resettlement sites were used to set up village enterprises paying the villagers a yearly share. It also records that the transitional fees for displaced families were first paid monthly, that this was not convenient for some of them, and that after an internal review the fees were changed to a yearly payment. Grievances were taken by the village committee, the district and the project office's resettlement agency, by telephone or in person. Individual family tombs along the road alignment were relocated; the Bank's cultural resources adviser agreed they had no archaeological, palaeontological, architectural, religious, aesthetic or cultural significance, and their relocation was handled under the resettlement policy rather than the cultural property policy. The Bank concluded that its policy on indigenous peoples did not apply: Xining has 38 ethnic minorities making up 26 per cent of its population, but in Chengbei District, where the completion report says the entire project was located, over 90 per cent of the population is Han.
xining-wusixi-road-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,444 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The nearest figures in the Bank's documents are the appraisal estimates of 1,921 people in 481 households affected by land acquisition and 527 people in 121 households displaced by housing demolition, which come to 2,448; no document found states 2,444. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review both reprint the appraisal's 121 households and 527 individuals, and both keep the appraisal's forward-looking verb - the Evaluation Group writes that the project's investments 'involved displacing 121 households (527 individuals)'. Neither gives an outcome count of anyone moved. The outcome figures that do exist are areas, in the updated resettlement action plan of January 2018: 233,600 square metres of structures demolished and 724.88 mu of land acquired by 31 December 2016, against 150,661 square metres and 788.09 mu planned. No Bank document found gives a count of people or households actually relocated under the project.
xining-wusixi-road-demolition.outcome: The loan closed on 30 August 2021. The completion report says all three resettlement complexes were finished before closing and that each family received at least two apartments. The gap between the demolition, finished on 31 December 2016, and the start of the last complex, which had not begun in January 2018, is recorded only in the updated resettlement action plan; neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's review mentions the delay or says when the Huangzhong County complex was finished.

xining-wusixi-road-demolition.confidence_note: The three-year delay in building the replacement housing, and the one complex not started a year after the houses came down, rest on a single source: the updated resettlement action plan of January 2018, prepared by the Xining project office and the consulting agency it hired, and disclosed by the Bank. Its demolition and land figures are attributed to the external monitoring agency's report, which is not in the Bank's public archive. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review do not mention the delay. No independent account of this resettlement was found; two searches, one of them in Chinese, returned nothing on these works. No document found says how many households were waiting at any of the three complexes, how long any family waited, or what the transitional fee was worth. The completion report's own account is favourable throughout: all sites completed before the loan closed, at least two apartments per family, no disruption to original neighbourhoods, savings turned into village enterprises, and the transitional fee changed on request. The project did not finance the land acquisition; the city paid for it. The 760 households resettled in 2010 to 2012, and the 520,487 square metres of houses demolished then, were carried out before the project was identified and are not counted here as the project's doing. The date on the completion report's cover page is 22 February 2022; the Bank's archive record field gives it as 22 February 2021.
xining-wusixi-road-demolition.conditions: The project was environmental category B and triggered the policies on involuntary resettlement and physical cultural resources; the policy on indigenous peoples was not triggered. A resettlement action plan and a resettlement policy framework were prepared by the project office, disclosed and accepted by the Bank, and the plan was updated in January 2018 for the works added by the restructuring. The appraisal document records that the due diligence review of the 2010 to 2012 land acquisition and resettlement, carried out before the project was identified, concluded that it complied with Chinese land law and Qinghai provincial and local regulation and that living conditions had been restored in compliance with the substantive aspects of the Bank's resettlement policy. The second kind of land take, under the project and its linked activities, was to be covered by the plan and the framework for all acquisition and resettlement taking place before the loan closed. Grievances were to be taken by the village committee, the district and the project office's resettlement agency. The Project Agreement for Loan 8319-CN, dated 4 March 2014, is published only as a scanned image with no text layer, so its covenants were not read (Project Appraisal Document, 20 November 2013; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 22 February 2022; Resettlement Action Plan, January 2018).

nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.title: Three Thousand Households Moved Off the Nanjiangbin Road Alignment on Nantai Island
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.place: The Nanjiangbin Road alignment on the south bank of the Min River near Fanchuanpu, Cangshan District, Nantai Island, Fuzhou, Fujian, China
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.point: Fanchuanpu Cathedral, Cangshan District, Fuzhou, whose administration building stood on the optimal alignment for Nanjiangbin Road and was moved to clear it; the slum of 3,000 households lay along the same alignment (OpenStreetMap point for Fanchuanpu Cathedral)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-48120 for the Fuzhou Nantai Island Peri-Urban Development Project (P070519). US$100 million, approved 15 December 2005, effective 16 February 2007, of which US$92.93 million was disbursed and US$6.33 million cancelled at the second restructuring. Environmental category A. Original closing 30 June 2011; actual closing 31 May 2013 after restructurings on 14 June 2011, which extended the loan by 21 months, and 19 March 2013, which added two months. The loan financed three road works on Nantai Island - Nanjiangbin Road, a 4.1 km riverside road along the south bank of the Min River with a 1.1 km approach to the Qianheng Bridge and local roads; the 11.6 km southern section of the Third Ring Road; and the Kuiqi Bridge, a cable-stayed crossing of the Min River - together with a public transport component including the Jinshan Bus Depot and a pilot bus priority lane, and technical assistance. The completion report rated outcome Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Low, Bank performance Satisfactory and borrower performance Satisfactory, and rated social safeguards Moderately Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review, posted 20 June 2014, agreed on outcome, Bank performance and borrower performance but gave risk to development outcome as Moderate rather than Low (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR2906, 11 November 2013; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, China - Fuzhou Nantai Island Peri-urban Development Project).

companies.name: Fuzhou Development and Reform Commission
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet - the Fuzhou municipal body that approves and programmes public investment, under the Fuzhou Municipal Government. The completion report attributes the decisions on resettlement to the Fuzhou Municipal Government itself, which chose to move the whole slum and then wrote the practices used into a new city resettlement policy. The project agreement also names unspecified 'Project Companies' through which Fuzhou was to carry out parts of the works (Project Agreement for Loan 4812-CN, 21 November 2006; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 11 November 2013).

nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.community: Nanjiangbin Road was laid along the south bank of the Min River on Nantai Island, through a slum of 3,000 households, about 10,000 people, mostly wage workers on limited incomes. The completion report describes the housing as poor quality and of marginal market value, typically built with rudimentary methods and unreliable materials, many lacking a kitchen or a toilet. The road alignment itself affected 480 households. After multiple consultations, and following the community's request, the Fuzhou Municipal Government decided to resettle the entire population of 3,000 households. The original relocation site had to be expanded and redesigned and new funds found for transitional support to each household. In total 4,642 new apartments were built for the community, with a few households taking cash compensation instead or moving earlier into existing apartments. The completion report says ex-post interviews revealed high levels of satisfaction, that the size and quality of the new apartments were a significant improvement, and that unlike their former homes the new apartments are household assets that can be sold. The project's resettlement also ran years late. In the first two years the project was held up mainly by resettlement; by the mid-term review of 2 December 2009 only US$20.562 million of the US$100 million loan had been disbursed against US$50 million expected. Two problems were outstanding at that point: the Jinshan Bus Depot had not started because land acquisition kept being delayed, and as the Kuiqi Bridge works progressed the land for building resettlement houses for the people affected by its northern section remained unavailable. The completion report says progress on resettlement was slow, that the delays came from lengthy negotiations with affected populations, and that consultations with all the displaced populations and villagers revealed most people were satisfied with their new situations. It rates social safeguards Moderately Satisfactory, stating that although the outcome was satisfactory the considerable delays and additional costs in resettlement brought the rating down. The first restructuring extended the loan by 21 months to finish the Kuiqi Bridge, the Third Ring Road and the Jinshan Bus Depot. At project closing the Jinshan Bus Depot had reached only 35 per cent of its construction targets, after a land acquisition process the report calls slow and very difficult, which caused almost two years of delay. Four non-motorised transport access ramps to the Kuiqi Bridge were still unbuilt at closing because the resettlement they needed, minor in scope, was delayed, and the municipal government could offer no estimate of when they would be finished. The administration building of Fanchuanpu Cathedral, a provincial cultural heritage site standing on the best alignment for the road, was lifted whole - a 1,500 tonne structure built in 1929 - moved 89 metres sideways, rotated 90 degrees and moved another 30 metres.
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.displaced_label: households resettled from the slum on the Nanjiangbin Road alignment, of which 480 households were directly affected by the alignment itself (World Bank completion report, 11 November 2013)
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,927 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved; no figure of 1,927 was found in any Bank document opened. The completion report puts the slum at 3,000 households and 10,000 inhabitants, says the road alignment affected 480 of those households, and says the municipal government resettled all 3,000. The Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats the same figures. Neither document gives a count of people, as against households, actually moved, and neither breaks the 3,000 households down by the terms they took.
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.outcome: The loan closed on 31 May 2013 with US$6.33 million cancelled, the Jinshan Bus Depot 35 per cent built and the Kuiqi Bridge's non-motorised access ramps unbuilt because the resettlement for them was delayed. The completion report said the depot would be finished by March 2014 and could give no date for the ramps. The practices used in the Nanjiangbin Road resettlement were adopted by the Fuzhou Municipal Government as a new city resettlement policy, which the completion report calls a benchmark for other Chinese cities.

nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.confidence_note: Both Bank documents treat this resettlement as a success, and what follows here should be read against that. The completion report says the resettlement plan and policy framework were carried out without any major complaints, that ex-post interviews with resettled people showed a high level of satisfaction, that the new apartments were a significant improvement on the slum housing, that most people were satisfied with their new situations, and that the land acquisitions were in the end completed satisfactorily and without major complaints. The move was made at the community's request and only 480 of the 3,000 households stood in the road's path. What is documented against that is delay: a resettlement that held the project up for its first two years, land for replacement houses on the Kuiqi Bridge's northern section unavailable at the mid-term review, a social safeguards rating cut to Moderately Satisfactory for considerable delays and additional costs, a bus depot 35 per cent built after almost two years of land acquisition delay, and access ramps left unbuilt at closing with no date. No document found counts the households caught in those delays or says how long any of them waited. Every figure comes from the Bank's own completion report, the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it and the project agreement; the lender is reporting on its own project, and no independent account was found. The resettlement action plan itself was not among the documents read. The completion report carries two dates of its own: 11 November 2013 on the cover page and 7 November 2013 in its data sheet.
nanjiangbin-road-slum-resettlement-fuzho.conditions: The project was environmental category A and triggered the policies on involuntary resettlement and cultural property. A resettlement action plan was prepared for Nanjiangbin Road and the Third Ring Road, and a resettlement policy framework for the project as a whole, to guide a plan for the Kuiqi Bridge and the Jinshan Bus Depot, whose alignment and location were not settled at appraisal. The Project Agreement for Loan 4812-CN, dated 21 November 2006, required Fuzhou to take all necessary actions to minimise to the extent possible any involuntary loss by persons of shelter, productive assets, access to productive assets, income or means of livelihood, temporarily or permanently; to implement, and cause Fuzhou and the Project Companies to implement, the resettlement action plan and the resettlement policy framework in a manner satisfactory to the Bank; and to furnish any proposed modification or waiver of either to the Bank for concurrence before putting it into effect. It also required policies and procedures adequate to monitor and evaluate the plans, including the engagement of experienced and qualified independent monitoring agencies acceptable to the Bank, and a resettlement specialist and an environmental specialist on the implementation team (Project Agreement, 21 November 2006; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 11 November 2013).

shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.title: Village Land and Houses Taken for Shangrao Sanqingshan Airport
shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.place: Zunqiao town, Guangxin District (formerly Shangrao County), Shangrao, Jiangxi, China
shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.point: Zunqiao town, which the completion report calls the town most affected by resettlement under the project (OpenStreetMap town point for Zunqiao, Guangxin District, Shangrao)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-82560 for the Jiangxi Shangrao Sanqingshan Airport Project (P123729). US$50 million, approved 13 May 2013, effective 16 July 2013, revised to US$49,393,873 and that amount disbursed. Environmental category A, full assessment. Closed 31 December 2018, on its original closing date, with no restructuring. Total project cost rose from US$105.13 million at appraisal to US$125.46 million, the borrower's own contribution rising from US$55.13 million to US$76.07 million; of about RMB478 million in counterpart funding, RMB350 million came as a grant from China's Civil Aviation Development Fund. The loan financed a 4C-level airfield - runway, taxiway and associated works - a terminal building and apron, installation works and technical assistance. The completion report of 25 June 2019 rated outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and quality of monitoring and evaluation Substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, dated 30 September 2019 in the Bank's archive record, rated both outcome and Bank performance Highly Satisfactory, a grade above the completion report on each, and agreed on monitoring and evaluation at Substantial (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 25 June 2019; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, CN-Shangrao Sanqingshan Airport Project).

companies.name: Shangrao Sanqingshan Airport Construction Office
companies.role: The implementing agency named in the completion report's data sheet, the project management office set up by the Shangrao Municipal Government to build the airport. The completion report credits the municipal government with formulating and approving the policies for resettlement and land acquisition and issuing the necessary legal documents, and with building the 4.65 km access road to the airport and its utilities outside the project with its own money (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 25 June 2019).

companies.name: Jiangxi Airport Group
companies.role: The provincial airport operator, which runs all seven airports in Jiangxi. The Shangrao Municipal Government signed an operational concession agreement with it to operate the airport, in consultation with the Civil Aviation Administration of China, in place of the management consultancy the project had originally planned (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 25 June 2019).

companies.name: Shangrao Sanqingshan Airport Company Limited
companies.role: The airport company named in the completion report's list of abbreviations as the body the project was to support with a human resources plan and an operational and financial manual; that consultancy was cancelled when the concession to the Jiangxi Airport Group was adopted instead (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 25 June 2019).

shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.community: The project built a new feeder airport on farmland outside Shangrao. The completion report gives the outcome of the land take: the project required the acquisition of 2,913 mu of village land, which the Independent Evaluation Group's review converts to 194 hectares, and the demolition of 7,708 square metres of existing structures of 21 affected households. The report says these impacts were slightly higher than planned, on the basis of detailed measurements taken during implementation. At appraisal the figures had been 150 hectares of village land, including 26 hectares of cultivated land, affecting some 2,500 people from 500 households, and the demolition of 5,760 square metres of structures affecting 76 people from 16 households. Resettlement activities started in 2013 and were completed by the end of 2018, the month the loan closed. Field surveys found 137 household graves on the airport site; their relocation was compensated under the resettlement action plan. The project also interrupted local rural roads and irrigation systems, which the resettlement plan covered, and the appraisal noted that noise from the airport in operation might be unavoidable for local people. Both documents report the outcome favourably. The completion report says resettlement monitoring showed affected people have better housing, including better infrastructure such as water, drainage and community services, and that semi-annual external monitoring confirmed land acquisition and compensation were carried out in accordance with the resettlement plans. The Evaluation Group's review adds that there were no delays in the payment of appropriate compensation. A 2016 consultant survey of 30 affected households in Zunqiao town, the town the completion report says was most affected by resettlement, found that between 2013 and 2015 average household income rose from RMB28,534 to RMB35,950, a growth of 26 per cent, average household living area rose from 388 to 472 square metres, and the share of agriculture in average household income fell from 12.9 to 10.4 per cent, which the report reads as affected villagers moving out of farming into airport work. The 4.65 km access road linking the airport to the nearest main road was built by the municipal government outside the project, and was brought inside the resettlement action plan for safeguards purposes.
shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,479 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved; no figure of 2,479 was found in any Bank document opened. The nearest appraisal figures are 'some 2500 people from 500 households' affected by the land acquisition and 76 people from 16 households affected by the structure demolition. The completion report's outcome figures are different and larger: 2,913 mu of village land acquired and 7,708 square metres of structures of 21 affected households demolished. The verb attached to the 21 households in both the completion report and the Evaluation Group's review is 'affected', not relocated, and no Bank document found gives a count of people or households actually relocated. The Evaluation Group's review states that the Bank project team supplied it with a detailed table comparing planned and actual land acquisition because the units differed between the appraisal document and the completion report; that table is not in any document found, and nothing from it is used here.
shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.outcome: The loan closed on 31 December 2018 on its original date, with the airport built and operating under a concession to the Jiangxi Airport Group. Resettlement activities were completed by the end of 2018. No document found records any outstanding compensation, grievance or unfinished resettlement.

shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.confidence_note: This is the thinnest of the six Chinese cases in this batch and the Bank's documents record no shortfall of any kind. What is documented is the land take itself: 2,913 mu, about 194 hectares, of village land acquired and 7,708 square metres of houses demolished, both larger than planned. Against that, the completion report says monitoring showed affected people have better housing with better water, drainage and community services, that compensation followed the resettlement plans, and that a survey of 30 households found incomes up 26 per cent over two years; the Evaluation Group's review says there were no delays in the payment of appropriate compensation and rates the whole project Highly Satisfactory. No document found counts anyone relocated, names any affected person, gives a compensation rate, or records a complaint, a grievance or a late payment. The income survey covers 30 households out of the hundreds affected and was carried out by a consultant for the project. Every figure comes from the Bank's own completion report, the Evaluation Group's review of it and the appraisal document; no independent account was found, and two searches, one of them in Chinese, returned nothing on these works. The Evaluation Group's review prints no date anywhere on the page; the date given for it is the Bank archive's own record field, which is not verified on the document itself.
shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.conditions: The project was environmental category A with a full assessment and triggered the policies on environmental assessment, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement. A resettlement action plan and a resettlement policy framework were prepared and approved by the Bank in 2012, before appraisal, and disclosed to local people on 20 September 2012, with English versions sent to the Bank's InfoShop on 30 October 2012. The policy framework was prepared because the exact locations of the airport road and other facilities had not been fixed. The 4.65 km access road, paid for by the Shangrao Municipal Government outside the project, was included in the resettlement action plan for safeguards purposes. The Project Agreement for Loan 8256-CN, dated 4 June 2013, required the project implementing entity to implement the safeguards instruments in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Bank, barred any amendment or waiver of them without the Bank's prior written agreement, and required reporting on the status of compliance with them; where the agreement's provisions conflicted with the safeguards instruments, the latter prevailed. Grievances could be filed orally or in writing with resettlement offices at all levels, and the completion report records that women's views and concerns on resettlement were collected and analysed during both the preparation and the implementation of the plan (Project Agreement, 4 June 2013; Project Appraisal Document, 16 April 2013; Implementation Completion and Results Report, 25 June 2019).
